projects.name: National capacities supported and strengthened to effectively prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons in accordance with international standards and best practices, and to achieve sustainable impact through implementation of the National Action Plan against TiP
projects.description:
UNODC has been engaged with the Saudi Human Rights Commission (HRC), as chair entity of the National Committee to Combat Human Trafficking (NCCHT) since February 2020 in a multi-phased project of technical cooperation in the field of combating trafficking in persons (TiP). Therethrough, UNODC supports national efforts spearheaded by the HRC/NCCHT in preventing and combating TiP through a victim-centred approach that upholds the rights of trafficked and potential victims to protection, support, and care in line with international standards and norms and best practices.
Achievements under Phase I (February 2020 - August 2022) include the launch of the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) on 31 March 2020 which is currently managed by a central team in Riyadh together with 13 sub-teams in all regions across the Kingdom for effective coordination in dealing with TiP cases; the establishment of TiP specialized courts in all regions of the Kingdom with 124 prosecutors; the creation of the first-ever anti-TiP specialized Prosecution Unit on 30 July 2022; the creation of a specialized TiP Data Management Team; the development and adoption of the National Action Plan to Combat TiP (2021-2023); the legislative review and reform of the Kafala sponsorship system; and the delivery of 33 capacity-building activities that benefited over 1,600 officials within government entities, institutions, and CSOs.
Phase II (3 years, launched in March 2023) focuses on sustaining the outcomes of Phase I and further supporting the Kingdom through the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) against TiP. Activities include reviewing and updating the NRM; developing the electronic format of the NRM to support the availability, accuracy, and timeliness of TiP-related data; building monitoring and evaluation capacities for the implementation of the NAP; raising awareness of labour dispute committees, the media, the private sector and through religious authorities; conducting legislative and policy reviews; strengthening national capacities of law enforcement and criminal justice for the investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of TiP cases; supporting the creation of a national training resource/hub on preventing and combating TiP; and promoting the creation of partnerships for knowledge and best practices exchange.

framework.name: People — According to the principles of ‘Leave No One Behind’ (LNOB), ensure that all human beings can fulfil their potential in dignity, equity, and equality in a healthy environment (SDGs 1–5)
framework.description: The achievement of SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDG/SDR 1 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 2 indicators prevalence of undernourishment and cereal yield have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 3 indicators maternal mortality rate, neonatal mortality rate, mortality rate, under-five mortality rate, incidence of tuberculosis, adolescent fertility rate, births attended by skilled health personnel, surviving infants who received two WHO-recommended vaccines, and subjective well-being have been achieved. The SDG/SDR 4 indicators net primary enrolment rate, lower secondary completion rate, and literacy rate have been achieved. No SDG/SDR 5 indicators have been reported in the data as achieved as of 2021.

framework.name: Planet — Protect the planet from degradation, including through sustainable consumption and production, sustainably manage its natural resources, and take urgent action on climate change (SDGs 6, 12–15)
framework.description: The SDG/SDR 6 indicators that face major challenges are freshwater withdrawal, anthropogenic wastewater that receives treatment, and scarce water consumption embodied in imports. The SDG/SDR 12 indicator that faces major challenges is electronic waste. The SDG/SDR 13 indicators that face major challenges are CO₂ emissions from fossil fuel combustion and cement production and CO₂ emissions embodied in imports. The SDG/SDR 14 indicators that face major challenges are mean area protected in marine sites important to biodiversity and Ocean Health Index. The SDG/SDR 15 indicators that face major challenges are mean area protected in terrestrial sites important to biodiversity and mean area protected in freshwater sites important to biodiversity.

framework.name: Prosperity — Ensure that all human beings can enjoy prosperous and fulfilling lives (SDGs 7–11)
framework.description: The SDG/SDR 7 indicators population with access to electricity and population with access to clean fuels and technology for cooking have been achieved. No SDG/SDR 8 indicators have been achieved as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicators population using the internet, mobile broadband subscriptions, Logistics Performance Index: quality of trade and transport-related infrastructure, and Times Higher Education Universities Ranking: average score of top 3 universities have been achieved. The achievement of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. No SDG/SDR 11 indicators have been achieved as of 2021 as per available data. No SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDGs 7 or 8 face major challenges as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicator that faces major challenges is expenditure on research and development. The assessment of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 11 indicator that faces major challenges is annual mean concentration of particulate matter of less than 2.5 microns in diameter.
